title: La piscine de François  (François's Swimming Pool)

segments.t: Andréa drives out to François Berléand's country house to make peace after his violent fight with Christophe Bel. Climbing over the garden wall, she finds François digging a giant hole in his lawn and discovers a surprising secret that explains all his fears. Let's listen to the scene in French first.
François, c'est moi. Je suis là, comme prévu.
Ça suffit! Fox, du calme!
Je fais creuser une piscine.
Sans blague?
Je ne supporte plus la honte de ne pas savoir nager.
J'ai refusé tellement de films.
Lesquels? Titanic?
Je suis fière de toi, François.
Je suis vraiment désolée pour Dom Juan.
Je sais que Christophe Bel a de la vision.
Tu vas le faire, alors?
Non, c'est trop tard maintenant.
Christophe le regrette aussi. Il t'admire, tu le sais!
Alors pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
Christophe? C'est Andréa Martel.
J'espère que tu es libre ce soir, je t'invite à dîner.
D'accord, avec plaisir.
François shares his private secret. Let us examine the lines with English notes.

'François, it is me. I am here, as planned.' Andréa announces her arrival at the country house.

'That is enough! Fox, quiet!' François calms his barking terrier dog Fox. François pairs the verb meaning 'is enough' with the noun for 'calm'.
Je fais creuser une piscine.
'I am having a swimming pool dug.' François opens with the word for 'am having' and lands on 'swimming pool' at the close.
Sans blague?
'Seriously?' Andréa opens with the word for 'joke' and lands on 'joke' at the close.
Je ne supporte plus la honte de ne pas savoir nager.
'I cannot take the shame of not knowing how to swim anymore.' Listen for the expression meaning 'no', which leads naturally into 'swim'.
J'ai refusé tellement de films.
'I have turned down so many films.' The key word here means 'I have', paired with 'films' to make the point clear.

'Which ones? Titanic?' Andréa teases him with humor. Andréa opens with the word for 'which ones?' and lands on 'which ones?' at the close.

'I am proud of you, François.' Andréa opens with the word for 'am' and lands on 'proud' at the close.

'I am really sorry about Dom Juan.' The key word here means 'am', paired with 'sorry' to make the point clear.
Je sais que Christophe Bel a de la vision.
'I know that Christophe Bel has vision.' Notice how the verb for 'know' leads straight into 'vision'.

'Are you going to do it, then?' Andréa encourages him to reconsider the role.
Non, c'est trop tard maintenant.
'No, it is too late now.' François hesitates out of wounded pride. The key word here means 'no', paired with 'now' to make the point clear.
Christophe le regrette aussi. Il t'admire, tu le sais!
'Christophe regrets it too. He admires you, you know that!' Andréa opens with the word for 'regrets' and lands on 'know' at the close.
Alors pourquoi il ne m'appelle pas directement?
'Then why does he not call me directly?' The key word here means 'then', paired with 'directly' to make the point clear.
Christophe? C'est Andréa Martel.
'Christophe? It is Andréa Martel.' Andréa takes initiative right away and dials his number.
J'espère que tu es libre ce soir, je t'invite à dîner.
'I hope you are free tonight, I am inviting you to dinner.' Andréa opens with the word for 'I hope' and lands on 'have dinner' at the close.
D'accord, avec plaisir.
